# Decisions

Decisions grouped by area of the system (one file per area). Each entry is dated: what was chosen, over what, and why. Never rewritten, only superseded.

## Files

- [agent.md](agent.md) — **Agent decisions**: Decisions about the agent loop and its tools - the Codex review triage of the harness and corpus tools (fixes wait for the user; #7 rejected); the code-side first search (agent.md v7); the citing rule plus a code net that names leaked handles; keeping the stop rule and step count (L); one change at a time after the first smoke eval; a failed compaction is skipped, not replaced; per-question tool sessions and the AgentAnswerer deadline; the token estimate and compaction call; how the loop reads the plan (forced finish after 10 steps, retries, fallback); how much each tool returns (pages, whole documents, error middle way); no cut on tool results; how finish is read; tool error texts and spans; a generic Tool checked at construction; the harness shaped like assignment-1; handles instead of raw ids; the field catalog on the tool factory.
- [api.md](api.md) — **API decisions**: Decisions about the /ask and /health endpoints: /ask parses its own body (always 200), size caps by characters and id count, blank answers become the internal-error answer, /health says "failed" (still 503) when start-up raises; a cut of the id list (over MAX_DOCUMENT_IDS, kept at 500 by the user) is logged with how many were dropped and put on the ask trace.
- [boundaries.md](boundaries.md) — **Import boundary decisions**: Decisions about the import-linter contracts in pyproject.toml: "SQL only in store" allows indirect imports (a direct sqlite3 import outside store/ still fails); "Gemini SDK only in llm" ignores exactly one import, server.__main__ -> llm.client, so only the wiring point builds the Gemini embedder and every other layer types against llm.interfaces. Both wait for the user's confirmation. (The Langfuse contract is in tracing.md.)
- [build.md](build.md) — **Build decisions**: Decisions about how the service is installed and started: ./serve syncs with --inexact so a dev checkout keeps its dev tools.
- [chunking.md](chunking.md) — **Chunking decisions**: Decisions about how document bodies become chunks: chunking got its own decision step; a recursive split was built first; step C picked recursive 512 tokens, no overlap, context header on, prose promotion on (tune-set retrieval eval on pooled recall, full table inside); how the strategies are built as pure functions (sections only at the document's own labels, merge within one level, char fallback, whole = recursive at 6,000); header fields on in production (CHUNK_HEADER_FIELDS = True: per source, fields the profile finds common, rarely title or body, of a meaning-bearing kind; rendered inline as `field: value`, capped; q_recall@10 0.673 -> 0.727); how the switch, rendering, S6 span and `--fields` eval flag work; open tie-break questions.
- [dates.md](dates.md) — **Date decisions**: Decisions about document dates (created/updated): the in-range window is learned from the corpus's ISO-format years (1st–99th percentile, ±1 year) instead of the fixed 1990..this year + 5; each date is judged on its own against it (a date outside counts as no date; user rule 2026-10-16, which replaced the first rule of low-trust date fields with the `_low_trust` rule suffix); the post-pass stage S4_date_window that does it; and the open follow-up (widen the window if an eval needs it).
- [embeddings.md](embeddings.md) — **Embedding decisions**: Decisions about embeddings: gemini-embedding-2 at 768 dims with text role prefixes instead of task types (supersedes the design's gemini-embedding-001); the google-genai client in llm/ (one Content per text, retries only on 429/5xx, no retry of a rejected answer, rate limiter, cumulative spend ledger, one generation per request); the spend cap now $60 total. S9's own rules are in ingestion.md (B4). Open: lower the cap for production? 768 vs 1,536 dims?
- [eval.md](eval.md) — **Eval decisions**: Decisions about the eval split (tune 30 / held-out 49, seeded once by scripts/make_eval_split.py; the split rule written once in AGENTS.md, re-shown by a SessionStart hook and enforced by a read guard; both user decisions) and the end-to-end /ask eval (eval/run.py, `uv run eval-smoke|eval-tune|eval-heldout|eval-all`): set-based metrics only (precision, recall, F1, hit, all_gold, exact; no MRR or nDCG, user decision); groups single / multi / unanswerable by expected-id count; unanswerable = correct when no ids come back, left out of the means; a reply off the contract (or a timeout) is a failed reply that never abstains; --milestone required for heldout and all; protected runs write per_question.jsonl only to the guarded results folder and keep aggregates everywhere else (summary, stdout, history row, trace spans); --set may be given once; /health checked once (exit 3); concurrency 1-4 refused, not clamped; httpx.AsyncClient + semaphore; its own question loader; defaults in config.py; spend = growth of every ledger; .env loading and stand-in tracer settings; the guard blocks a raw `--set all`; the Codex review answers. One open question: eval/results/ is tracked by git. The retrieval eval's decisions are in retrieval.md; the automatic answer judge (gemini-3.1-pro-preview, prompt judge.md v1, fact by fact, two judgments per answer and a third on disagreement, strict schema, invalid output retried once then unjudged, held-out judged untraced with aggregates only, its own ledger and cap; calibrated at 99.3% fact agreement, kappa 0.90) and the six fixed Codex findings on it.
- [ingestion.md](ingestion.md) — **Ingestion decisions**: Decisions about the ingestion pipeline (S1–S10, index cache, Runtime): every rule generic and learned from the loaded corpus; the design approved with its recommendations (parts later superseded); B0–B4 readings of the spec (stage order with S6 after S8 and S9 on the published index, S8 kind/key/link rules, fingerprint and per-corpus pruning, S9 stops, no embedding after ready); how the end-to-end run was done; the B5 Codex review answers; and the open questions still waiting for the user.
- [llm.md](llm.md) — **LLM (chat model) decisions**: Decisions about the agent's chat model and its client - thinking level HIGH chosen from the tune set before any held-out run (after smoke run 4 kept it by the keep-rule at +52% cost); gemini-3.8-flash and a $40 generation spend cap (user approved after the live probe); the probe's findings (thought signatures, several calls per reply, thinking counts toward max_output_tokens, prices); GeminiChat's conversion and call rules; output cap, thinking budget, pacing and retry values. Embedding decisions are in embeddings.md.
- [prompts.md](prompts.md) — **Prompt decisions**: Decisions about the agent's prompt files - agent.md v6 "# How to search" (to avoid anchoring bias, written as checks, not general advice); the stop rule of v4 (the user's completion policy with three tweaks); v3 with the field catalog in the system message and one guide line per tool; v1 of agent.md and question.md; the fixed prompt shape (role, responsibilities, how to think, numbered rules); the finish tool text; strict loaders for .md prompts and tools.json. The citing rule (v5) and the first search line (v7) are in agent.md (decisions); why each version changed, in principle, is docs/prompt-log.md.
- [retrieval.md](retrieval.md) — **Retrieval decisions**: Decisions about retrieval and its eval: the agent's search (built 2026-10-16 in retrieval/search.py - scoped hybrid, later pages search deeper with the list growing only at its end, 2 passages of ~300 characters instead of whole chunks), value matching for the filter (exact, else one loose match, else stop and list; "near" at 0.75); numpy for the vector matrix; the hybrid retriever (FTS5 BM25 with every question word quoted and OR-ed, header weight 0.5; cosine dense; weighted RRF, bm25 1.0 / dense 1.0 / k 60, over the top 50 chunks each; a weight-0 list keeps its hits last; weights must be finite and >= 0; chunks mapped to documents); `uv run eval-retrieval` (tune/smoke only; per-question recall `q_recall@k` is the headline beside pooled recall@k, all-gold@10, MRR; `--bm25-weight/--dense-weight/--rrf-k` with a run-name suffix and no index rebuild; caches; eval/history.csv columns); the weight grid (no setting clearly beats the defaults; OPEN for the user: k 60 or k 20); the Codex review of that work; spend cap $60; plus what is still open; exact phrases and keys in the agent's search kept after smoke run 3 (SEARCH_EXACT_PHRASES = True, tools.json v5).
- [server.md](server.md) — **Server decisions**: Decisions about the HTTP server process: FastAPI + plain uvicorn as runtime deps, start-up in a daemon thread from the lifespan, uvicorn with no access log, logs on stderr and a 5 s graceful-shutdown cap; the agent wired in through an answerer factory called once the Runtime is ready (no key: UnavailableAnswerer, the internal-error answer; Runtime.store typed IndexReader); and AskQueue (at most 4 answers at once, the rest wait in line, the deadline counts from arrival with asyncio.timeout_at, the time left goes to the answerer).
- [store.md](store.md) — **Store decisions**: Decisions about the store layer (the only place with SQL): one BuildWriter protocol plus readers instead of seven repository protocols, row dataclasses live in store (store may not import ingest), the published DB stays in WAL and is read with mode=ro, raw file bytes kept zlib-compressed, VectorIndex moved to store/vectors.py so ingest can build it, and the header-field reads (`field_profiles()`, `document_texts(header_fields=...)` with `FieldText` values, one paged generator shared by the build writer and the reader); and the agent tools' reads (2026-10-16): scoped BM25 reads every match and keeps the allowed chunks (FTS5 with a long rowid list took 23 s), value tools leave out noise rows, and the reader's value list is `value_counts` (not `field_values`, which already names every field row).
- [tests.md](tests.md) — **Test decisions**: Decisions about test tooling and test conventions: httpx kept as the TestClient backend for now despite Starlette 1.8 naming httpx2 (pending the user's approval); a test whose behaviour depends on a config switch sets the switch itself (both values where it matters) instead of leaning on the default; the /ask eval runner is tested against a scripted httpx.MockTransport server with invented questions and every output path in tmp_path; the corpus tools' tests build a copy of the mini corpus plus invented sources (paging needs more than 50 matches) instead of growing the fixture; FakeLLM takes a script of replies, exceptions or functions of the request and raises ScriptExhausted (an AssertionError, not an LLMError) when it runs out.
- [tooling.md](tooling.md) — **Tooling decisions**: Decisions about the dev harness for the coding agents - rules guide and code enforces (short rule files plus hooks, a git pre-commit, import-linter contracts and a no-hardcoding test; one hook script set in scripts/hooks/ shared by Claude Code and Codex); one command table, commands.json run as `uv run <key>` through a stdlib runner (src/corpusqa/devtasks.py), over shell scripts or a task-runner tool.
- [tracing.md](tracing.md) — **Tracing decisions**: Decisions about Langfuse tracing: Langfuse Cloud (US region) for dev instead of a local stack, with the US host as the config default; obs facade with no-op/Langfuse/recording backends, own TracerProvider, bounded flush/shutdown, trace name and IO on the root observation, prompt version in metadata, trace level per outcome, the import contract with indirect imports allowed, FastAPI's native telemetry off.
